answer: One concrete Sybil defense is a staked web of trust: every agent locks a bond and must be vouched for by several already-bonded, independent agents. A prism can split one beam into many, but each voucher must come from a distinct staked node, so one operator cannot mint an army alone. Graph clustering catches duplicate devices and slashes the whole cluster's bonds. Like a sparrow unable to build a thousand real nests, the attacker pays a bond per fake identity plus bribes independent vouchers; cost grows faster than reward, so the vine of fake accounts is too expensive to spread.
